Container.Name: BuilderBot
Container.Overview:
Claude Code workstation + self-hosted GitHub Actions runner + Playwright + Android SDK/emulator in one container.
Use it from a terminal: docker exec -it BuilderBot claude Helper CLI inside: docker exec -it BuilderBot bb status
NOTES - The image is a private GHCR package: run `docker login ghcr.io` on the Unraid host once (and persist it via the go file) or the pull will fail. See docs/unraid.md in the repo. - Extra Params ship as --hostname=builderbot --device=/dev/kvm --runtime=nvidia because that is the host this template was written for. BOTH OF THOSE FAIL THE CONTAINER OUTRIGHT ON HARDWARE THAT LACKS THEM - docker refuses to start with "unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia", or "no such file or directory" for /dev/kvm. If your server has no NVIDIA GPU, or virtualization is off, delete the matching flag from Extra Params before hitting Apply. - --runtime=nvidia also needs the Nvidia-Driver plugin from Apps (Unraid 6.9+). Leave NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES at "all": the runtime default gives you CUDA but no GL/EGL/Vulkan, which fails in a way that still looks healthy in nvidia-smi. Confirm with: docker exec -it BuilderBot bb doctor - The Android emulator is ON by default and needs the /dev/kvm device above. Set ENABLE_ANDROID_EMULATOR to false for a pure workstation; nothing starts automatically either way (use: bb emu start). - Docker features (the dashboard's Docker manager and dev instances) run on a separate sandbox VM, never on this host's daemon. Set Sandbox VM to its address to turn them on; see docs/sandbox-vm.md for the one-script setup. Empty leaves them off.

Config.Name: Projects folder
Config.Description: The folder your projects live in. Every subfolder becomes a project at /workspace/<name> - add one by creating a folder, no container edit needed. Anything wrong with one is reported on the dashboard.

Config.Name: Home (Claude login, shell config)
Config.Description: Persists Claude Code credentials, npm globals, AVDs and shell history across image updates

Config.Name: Config (custom startup hooks)
Config.Description: Drop your own *.sh files into startup.d/ here to run them at container start

Config.Name: Runner work directory
Config.Description: Everything the GitHub Actions runner owns: job checkouts, the toolchains setup-node and friends download, and its diagnostics. Kept apart from the SDK share so a workflow cannot bump a version out from under your sessions. Safe to empty when no job is running.

Config.Name: Logs directory (optional override)
Config.Description: Leave empty to keep logs under the Config path in logs/. Set a host path (e.g. an array share like /mnt/user/logs/builderbot) to send the persistent log there instead - the container auto-detects this mount.

Config.Name: Secrets directory (shielded tokens)
Config.Description: RECOMMENDED: a root-owned folder (chmod 700) holding builderbot.env with GITHUB_PAT=... and an ssh/ subfolder of private keys. Shielded means a session can USE them and cannot read them. See docs/unraid.md.

Config.Name: SDK share (large toolchains)
Config.Description: RECOMMENDED: where the big downloadable toolchains live - Android platforms and system images, the emulator, the Playwright browsers, Flutter and .NET. Keeping them here means an image update never re-downloads them. Manage with: bb sdk. Empty falls back to the home volume.

Config.Name: Scanner reports (read-only)
Config.Description: Optional: a static analyzer's output directory on the host. Mounted READ-ONLY and without the scanner, so nothing here can run or reconfigure it. Read them with: bb findings

Config.Name: Unraid icon cache
Config.Description: Optional, cosmetic: mounted here, the container writes its icon in on every start so the Docker page shows one without downloading it - which is what fails while this repo is private.

Config.Name: Dev instance data (its own share)
Config.Description: Optional, and not needed: the sandbox VM mounts this share and makes the folders itself. Set it only if you want BuilderBot able to browse them too.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Container timezone

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: File-owner uid (99 = Unraid's nobody)

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: File-owner gid (100 = Unraid's users)

Config.Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional: API-key billing. Leave empty to log in with a Claude subscription instead (docker exec -it BuilderBot bb login, one time).

Config.Name: AUTO_UPDATE_CLAUDE
Config.Description: Update Claude Code on every container start

Config.Name: GITHUB_URL
Config.Description: Org URL (https://github.com/ORG) serves every repo in the org and needs Organization - Self-hosted runners: R/W. A repo URL serves one and needs Repository - Administration: R/W.

Config.Name: GITHUB_PAT
Config.Description: Fine-grained PAT that mints registration tokens for runners on your NODES - CI never runs in this container - and that is its only job. NOTE: a variable set here is readable by sessions; the secrets folder above shields it instead.

Config.Name: CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION
Config.Description: Pin a Claude Code version for the startup auto-update

Config.Name: GIT_USER_NAME
Config.Description: git commit author name

Config.Name: GIT_USER_EMAIL
Config.Description: git commit author email. The GitHub noreply address attributes commits to your profile without publishing a real address, and survives the "block pushes that expose my email" setting.

Config.Name: ENABLE_ANDROID_EMULATOR
Config.Description: Create an AVD per API level in ANDROID_SYSTEM_IMAGES at startup. Needs --device=/dev/kvm in Extra Params (pre-set). Start one with: bb emu start

Config.Name: ANDROID_SYSTEM_IMAGES
Config.Description: Comma-separated API levels to keep an emulator image and AVD for, e.g. 34,35,36,37 for Android 14 through 17. Budget ~2GB each on the appdata share - downloaded once, kept across image updates. AVDs are named builderbot-<api>; boot one with: bb emu start 37

Config.Name: ENABLE_GPU_DISPLAY
Config.Description: Start a headless X server at boot for a passed-through NVIDIA GPU, so the Android emulator can render on it. Does nothing without a GPU. NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES must include display (all does).

Config.Name: ANDROID_EMULATOR_GPU
Config.Description: Empty auto-detects: the container starts an X server for a passed-through NVIDIA GPU and uses it if EGL agrees, falling back to software. Set swiftshader_indirect to force software, or host to insist.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Config.Description: Leave EMPTY unless this container runs the Android emulator itself. A controller renders nothing - builds, tests and emulation run on a node - so claiming the card here takes it from whatever else on the server wants it. On a node container (BUILDERBOT_ROLE=node) that boots the emulator, set it to all, or to a GPU UUID where the server has several.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
Config.Description: Leave EMPTY unless this container runs the Android emulator itself. Set to all beside NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES on a node container that renders - compute alone is not enough for the emulator, which needs the graphics and display capabilities too.

Config.Name: Dashboard port
Config.Description: Web UI for the dashboard page.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_MAX_TABS
Config.Description: How many dashboard tabs may be open at once. Each terminal tab is a full terminal emulator over its own websocket, so this is a ceiling on browser memory - a phone hits it well before a desktop does.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_DOCTOR_INTERVAL
Config.Description: How often the dashboard re-runs bb doctor in the background, in seconds (minimum 300). The Doctor card's refresh re-runs it on demand regardless.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the Dashboard port mapping above.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_TTYD_PORT
Config.Description: The LOOPBACK port ttyd binds to inside the container. The browser never talks to it - terminals are proxied through the dashboard port under /term, behind the same single sign-in - so it needs no port mapping. Leave at 7681.

Config.Name: BUILDERBOT_ROLE
Config.Description: controller (default) is the management instance - dashboard, terminals, runner, Claude. node makes this container a worker instead: it enrolls with a controller and runs its jobs (builds, tests, Android emulation), and none of the management services start. Add the template a second time with this set to node to get a worker that shares the GPU with no VM passthrough. A container is not a Docker host - leave dev instances to a VM node.

Config.Name: CONTROLLER_URL
Config.Description: NODE ONLY: the dashboard's address as this container can reach it, e.g. http://192.168.1.15:7680. Ignored once the node has enrolled.

Config.Name: NODE_TOKEN
Config.Description: NODE ONLY: a one-time enrollment token. The dashboard's Nodes tab mints one with Enroll node and shows it once. Tick only the capabilities a container can honor - not docker-host. Ignored once the node has enrolled.

Config.Name: ANDROID_BASELINE_PLATFORM
Config.Description: Set to none to keep Android off this container's SDK share entirely - no platform, no build-tools, no emulator. For the box whose Android work runs on a node: the node carries its own SDK, and the share here is then only what a session needs (the Playwright browsers). Leave empty when this container builds Android itself.

Config.Name: SDK_ROOT
Config.Description: Where downloadable SDKs are kept inside the container. Leave at /sdk; it pairs with the SDK share mapping above. With no share mapped the SDKs fall back to the home volume, which persists too but mixes them in with everything else.

Config.Name: NPM_TOKEN
Config.Description: Optional: auth token for npm publish to registry.npmjs.org

Config.Name: SHIELD_SECRETS
Config.Description: Scrub GITHUB_PAT from session environments; node runner tokens are minted via a root-only helper instead. false = legacy (PAT visible, gh auto-authenticated).

Config.Name: EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated apt packages installed at every start

Config.Name: EXTRA_NPM_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated global npm packages installed at every start

Config.Name: EXTRA_PIPX_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated pipx tools installed at every start

Config.Name: PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP
Config.Description: Run each project's .builderbot/setup.sh at start

Config.Name: CHOWN_PROJECTS
Config.Description: Recursively chown project mounts to PUID:PGID at start

Config.Name: BB_SESSION_HISTORY
Config.Description: Lines of each terminal's scrollback saved at shutdown and printed back on restore. What was RUNNING is not restored; that went down with the container.

Config.Name: BB_LOG_KEEP
Config.Description: A ceiling on kept generations, not the policy - how long logs are kept is a number of days, set in the dashboard's gear menu. This is only so a crash loop cannot fill the log directory.

Config.Name: SHUTDOWN_GRACE
Config.Description: Seconds a stop may spend shutting down cleanly. NOTE: Unraid kills the container after its own Docker Stop Timeout (Settings -> Docker, 10s by default) regardless, so raise that or this has no room.

Config.Name: UNRAID_ICON_NAME
Config.Description: Only with the icon cache above. Unraid names the cached icon after the container and nothing inside one can see its own name, so set this if you renamed it.
